summary: Staggered-flush resonance causing p95/p99 latency plateaus for short streaming requests
description: Customer BrightWrite reports sustained p95/p99 latency plateaus on short streaming requests beginning 2026-03-10 08:00 UTC. Issue appears as repeated >500ms p95 and intermittent 2-4s p99 for 50-300 token streams. Preliminary traces point to flush alignment variability in the continuous batcher combined with periodic KV cache syncs, creating a resonant pattern of staggered flushes that elevates tail latency across tenant streams.
impact: Multiple API keys from BrightWrite experiencing degraded end-user latency on production dedicated capacity. Customer reports increased error-rate timeouts and UX regressions. No reported model output quality regressions. Billing unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send many short streaming requests (20-200 tokens) from multiple connections pinned to the BrightWrite tenant on prod:us-east-1.
2) Observe p95/p99 latency over a 10-20 minute window (heatmap shows periodic plateaus every ~60-90s).
3) Compare request-flush timestamps across worker processes; look for staggered flush groups that align with KV cache sync events.
observed_metrics: p99 generation latency spikes: 2.1-4.3 s intermittently
worker flush-count heatmap: rhythmic bands every 65-95s
KV cache sync spikes correlated with increased syscall time on GPU host during window
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:00 (Aisha): Initial customer report, captured trace IDs and sample payloads. Noted that affected requests are short streaming interactions (chat-like).

2026-03-10 10:15 (Marco): Pulled worker-level heatmaps; identified periodic banding in flush frequency across multiple worker pods tied to same shard. Bands coincide with KV cache maintenance window in runtime (approx every 70s).

2026-03-10 11:40 (Liu Chen): Reproduced locally in staging using scripted short-stream load generator with KV sync enabled. Disabling KV sync removes rhythmic plateaus. Hypothesis: KV sync introduces transient jitter that desynchronizes batching timers; micro-heterogeneity causes staggered flush groups and increased queueing for short streams.
2026-03-11 02:20 (Marco): Observed tenant-fairness mechanism tries to rebalance but interacts poorly with flush jitter leading to resonance (constructive interference) for tenants with medium QPS.

2026-03-12 04:05 (SRE): CPU syscalls during KV sync spike on host, causing small delays in batching loop wakeups. When multiple workers wake at slightly different offsets, flushes bunch into staggered groups that lengthen waiting time for some short requests.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Applied throttled KV-sync rollout on affected shard to reduce amplitude of sync-induced jitter.
2) Enabled per-tenant micro-coalescing guard to prioritize already-started streams for next flush (reduces queueing for short requests).

root_cause: Interaction between periodic KV cache synchronization and the continuous batcher's timer wakeups. KV sync causes short syscall/CPU jitter on worker hosts; small offsets across workers cause staggered flush groups that resonate with tenant traffic patterns and increase tail latency for short streaming requests.
resolution_notes: Mitigations deployed: 1) KV-sync smoothing throttled and staged rollout (runtime PR #4821), 2) per-tenant micro-coalescing guard enabled to prefer open streams at flush time, 3) added jitter-resistant batching-loop backoff. BrightWrite reports >70% reduction in p99 spikes after partial rollout. Full rollout scheduled pending additional telemetry.
